items.claim: Default CA load can prevent Requests import
items.consequence: Because adapters is imported by requests.sessions and requests imports sessions from its public package initializer, this CA load runs during every `import requests`. If the default bundle is missing, unreadable, malformed, or unavailable through packaged-path extraction, that import fails before callers can use HTTP, verify=False, or a custom CA path. It also adds synchronous bundle I/O to imports that never make a verified HTTPS request.
items.proposed_fix: Initialize and cache the default SSL context lazily on the first verified HTTPS request, with thread-safe one-time initialization, so loading the CA bundle remains on the request path.

native_payload.intent: Reuse a module-level urllib3 SSL context with the default CA bundle for ordinary verified requests, avoiding repeated CA loading while preserving Requests’ certificate verification behavior. Custom CA bundle files and directories and zipapp behavior are also intended to remain supported.

residual_risks: The process-wide preloaded SSLContext is mutable through urllib3 pool internals; trusted in-process code that mutates a pool's context could affect other adapters sharing it. This requires private transport access and was not treated as a user-triggerable defect.
The import-time startup cost depends on the platform CA bundle, filesystem, and SSL implementation; cold imports were not benchmarked against the prior revision.
testing_gaps: Add focused regression coverage that ordinary verify=True requests reuse the preloaded context while verify=False and custom trust remain isolated, and that the changed CA-directory branch works. Existing tests exercise verify=False and CA files but do not directly assert context reuse or cover CA directories (tests/test_requests.py:2833-2862, 2897-2927).
Exercise default CA bundle extraction/loading in a packaged or zipapp-style install; this import-time path now depends on the extracted bundle being available.
No import-time performance measurement was run; the reported cold-start cost is the synchronous CA bundle load introduced at module initialization.
